raw_response:
Well, it's early October now. Just finished getting the maize off most of my land last week. I've been farming for 25 years — since I was 24 — and I know this land pretty well. I only finished primary school, so I don't do fancy calculations, but I watch, I remember, and I talk to my neighbors. That's how I decide.

I've got 90 mu total. That's a good-sized piece, more than most in my village, but it's still me and my wife doing the daily work. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in Handan, and my younger brother helps when he's not off doing construction. They send money home, which helps, but it means I have to hire hands for the busy times. Can't do it all alone.

**Winter wheat:** I'll plant about 70 mu with wheat, same as last year. I buy improved seed — Jimai 22, costs about 35 yuan per mu. I don't trust saved seed for too many years; the yield drops. For fertilizer, when I plant in early October, I put down about 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind. That's my base. Then in spring, when the wheat greens up, I topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. At jointing, if the wheat looks a bit yellow — and it usually does — I put another 10 kg of urea. My neighbor Lao Zhang tried cutting back on fertilizer last year to save money, and his wheat was shorter. He regretted it. I'm not making that mistake. I irrigate three times: winter irrigation if the soil's dry, then at jointing, and at grain filling. The well water isn't free — electricity for the pump costs me maybe 30-40 yuan per mu for the season — but you can't skip it. For weeds, I spray herbicide in spring, and if aphids show up, I use insecticide. After maize harvest, I hire a rotary tiller — no time for deep plowing, got to get wheat in quick. My wife and I handle the fertilizing and watching, but for harvest I hire a combine and some village workers. If the weather's normal, I expect about 450 kg per mu.

**Summer maize:** Same 70 mu, planted right after wheat harvest in mid-June. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days. I buy hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. It's more expensive, but hybrid maize pays for itself. I barely till — one pass with the rotary tiller, then plant. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 30 kg per mu, and at big trumpet stage I side-dress with about 20 kg of urea. Irrigate once or twice, usually at jointing and if August is dry, at filling. Spray herbicide at planting, and watch for corn borer — if I see them, I spray insecticide. Less labor than wheat, but I still hire help for harvest. Should get around 480 kg per mu.

**Stevia:** I keep 20 mu for stevia. There's a buyer from Shandong who comes every fall, pays decent money for dried leaves. I buy improved seedlings — about 100 yuan per mu. I transplant in late April after the last frost. Stevia doesn't need as much nitrogen as grain — too much and the leaves get weak. I put base fertilizer at transplanting, maybe 25 kg compound per mu, then topdress after the first cut. Need to irrigate three times, carefully — stevia likes water but not waterlogged. Weeds are bad, so I use herbicide, and sometimes leaf spot comes, so I might spray fungicide. This crop needs lots of hands — transplanting and picking leaves. I hire village women, pay by the day. Hope for about 100 kg dried leaves per mu.

**Money:** All told — seed, fertilizer, water, pesticide, hired labor — I'll spend about 50,000 yuan this year. That's a lot, but my son sent 30,000 home last year, and the stevia buyer pays cash. Still, I keep a reserve. My granddaughter starts middle school next year, and you never know when someone gets sick. I'm not trying anything new. I'll do what worked last year.
